text:
Sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog ranking quality. Krichene–Rendle show that negative sampling can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; low sampling variance does not remove this bias. [RecSys 2025 research](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) evaluates sampling reliability through resolution, fidelity, robustness and predictive power. Consequently, performance against 99 negatives should be interpreted as the pinned benchmark objective, without assuming equivalent full-catalog improvement. [Foundational analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

Popularity slices matter: a [2024 sequential recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds that aggregate metrics hide head/mid/tail imbalances; random negative sampling favors head items, while popularity-based alternatives can improve balance at an overall accuracy cost. [Subbiah et al. (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371) demonstrate benefits from correcting sampled rank estimates in WARP/LambdaRank training. These findings support rank-based diagnostics and popularity stratification, but do not establish that any particular diagnostic predicts successful interventions.

Proposed calibration protocol: construct chronological pseudo-held-out continuations solely within training histories, excluding those continuations from probe fitting and popularity counts; preserve official splits. Compare against popularity and last-item transition baselines. On a fixed, bounded user subset, measure sampled/full-catalog rank agreement, percentile ranks and top-10 failures; report category and popularity slice sizes with paired user-bootstrap uncertainty. Raw score margins depend on score scale, so accompany them with ranks. Before training changes, specify predicted effects of history truncation, order shuffling or component ablation, then check whether observed changes match. Treat these as diagnostic audits; retain pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 as the sole selection criterion and prelimit validation queries.
